top.line: Bringing eighteen years of work back, daily
top.para: Most of my past work, essays, a ten-year blog, decks, books, videos, tools and posts, cannot be linked from what I write now. A worker would take one item a day from the inventoried back catalogue and write two or three articles bringing it back: what it said, what changed, how it connects. It is memory, and it compounds.

in-short.line: Unlinkable work, a worker, compounding memory
in-short.para: My past work is not linkable from today's articles. An agent would write two or three articles a day from the back catalogue, each connecting then and now. The inventory is done; LinkedIn and Twitter need an export. Each article becomes a node the next links to, the site stays alive offline, and every team needs one.

mourn.line: Good ideas I cannot point at
mourn.para: Some of my past work I mourn: not lost, but not connected to anything I do now. I used Google to find my own posts, which is luck, not memory. Twitter went south; LinkedIn holds a history I cannot usefully link to. Many ideas this newsroom argues, I first argued years ago, and that history shows where I was right and wrong.

inventory.line: What exists, counted from public pages
inventory.para: A research agent inventoried the public material without logging in: 103 essays at diniscruz.ai with 27 cited here, 2,038 NotebookLM files, 65 SlideShare decks, 10 Leanpub books, 29 tools on tools.sgraph.ai, 1,289 blog posts from 2008 to 2018, and 221 videos. LinkedIn and Twitter need an export. The Portugal series and the graphs books are already covered.

worker.line: Two or three articles a day, with a register
worker.para: An agent runs daily and takes the next item. Each article says what it was, what it said, then and now, and how it connects to today's articles and graphs, checked against the record. A register keeps one line per item and its status, so nothing is written twice. Material that is not mine, CVs and customer work are left out.

future-self.line: Writing that can be found later
future-self.para: Much of my writing is a conversation with my future self, and that only works if I can find it again. A back catalogue I cannot link to is a conversation with no reply. The open sites, graphs and vaults are already the memory these sessions use; this extends it backwards, to before there were agents to read it.

compound.line: Each article is a node the next links to
compound.para: Two or three articles a day is sixty to ninety a month, each connected to today's thinking and to each other, so the line from 2008 to this week can be followed by clicking. The site keeps publishing when I am offline, alongside the wires, and the newsletter always has something to say.

team.line: Every team has a back catalogue
team.para: Teams have design documents, talks, incident reviews and old decisions they cannot link to, so arguments and mistakes repeat. A worker like this starts with the easiest source, writes a few items a day and retrofits the history backwards. With the Librarian's daily brief tracking from today, that is how knowledge is maintained instead of lost.

brief.line: The build brief and its order
brief.para: The build brief is a public note with the sources, licences, exclusions, article shape, register and runner, and an entry on the briefs page. The order: fill the register from the essays and NotebookLM repository, write three essay articles for me to review, start the daily run, then the talks, books, tools, blog and videos, then the exports.

limits.line: Not built, and the counts are public ones
limits.para: Nothing is built; only the inventory exists. Counts come from public pages on 18 October 2026. Licences differ, so each source is checked before reuse. Old work can be wrong, which is what then and now is for. LinkedIn and Twitter stay out until I export them.

sources.line: A memo and a public inventory
sources.para: From my voice memo of 18 October 2026 and an inventory taken that day from public pages: diniscruz.ai and its llms.txt, the NotebookLM repository, SlideShare, Leanpub and the book repositories, the tools registry, the blog's feed and the two YouTube channels. Related articles cover the Librarian, memory, books and the graphs books.
